generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science this shapes every evidence review and project. You reach past the discovery service into databases like SPORTDiscus and follow citation trails between trials, then refine the search with Boolean operators and limiters so the results stay manageable. You weigh each study against its currency, authority and relevance before using it, and you run the cycle again as the project develops. Each search makes the next one sharper.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students gather evidence on the same training method. One runs a single library search and uses the first studies he finds, without judging their quality. The other searches SPORTDiscus, traces a key trial's citations both ways, tightens the search with Boolean terms and a date limiter, then weighs each study against authority and relevance. His review ends up wider and better grounded, because he runs reaching, refining and judging as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, searching well is a continuing practice. You reach into databases and citation trails, refine for precision and recall, and judge each study against explicit criteria, on every review you run. Treated this way, your evidence is both comprehensive and defensible.

_items.text: That the three strands are running as one practice: reaching widely, controlling the search, and judging what it returns.
